angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 329,066 km at 180.07 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.5533 +/- 0.0381 mas (same row, RUWE 1.02): 180.07 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.473 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-264 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.484....8L/abstract): 329,066 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.496 +/- 0.013 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-264 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.484....8L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3660 +/- 80 K from Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-264 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.484....8L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-264 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.484....8L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-264.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.784, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
